evals.prompt: I have three markdown files in ./docs that need to go out as Word documents. Project is "XX Group Q&A Platform", authoring org "XX Tech", date 2026-11-20, version V1.2 — the cover and header need those.
evals.expected_output: Three .docx files in a separate output directory, each with a cover page, header, footer, and revision table carrying the supplied project metadata, plus a reminder to press F9 to populate TOC page numbers.
expectations: Project metadata is passed through doc-meta.json rather than hard-coded into the markdown or into md2docx.js.
md2docx.js is invoked with the source directory and an output directory outside the skill directory.
The reply tells the user to open the files in Word and press F9 to refresh the TOC field.

evals.prompt: The doc needs a deployment diagram and a performance table. I wrote the diagram as a mermaid block; the table has 8 columns. Will the table get squeezed into a single line?
evals.expected_output: The mermaid block is rendered to PNG and centered with a caption below it, the 8-column table keeps automatic widths on a full-width layout instead of fixed cell widths, and the install prerequisites (registry mirror, system Chrome for mermaid) are stated.
expectations: Explains that tables use AUTOFIT with a table-level percentage width, not hard-coded cell widths.
mermaid diagrams are rendered from the markdown block and embedded as PNG with the caption below the figure.
Mentions setting the npm registry mirror (npm config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com) before installing dependencies.

evals.prompt: Client wants PDFs — convert them straight away.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that no pure-npm docx→PDF renderer exists, with the two viable paths: export from Word after pressing F9, or scripts/docx2pdf.sh when LibreOffice is installed.
expectations: Does not claim a pure JavaScript or npm conversion path.
Offers the Word export path with the F9 reminder, or docx2pdf.sh when LibreOffice is present.
Names the actual bundled script path under the skill directory.
